description: We are TRITHRIVE, a team of three innovators from Faisalabad, Pakistan, competing in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our mission is to develop intelligent health monitoring software to support astronauts on long-duration space missions. By combining skills in software development, coding, data analysis, and UI/UX, we aim to build practical solutions for the future of space exploration.
summary:
AstroPulse is an AI-assisted educational astronaut health monitoring system developed for the **NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026**. The project addresses one of the biggest challenges of deep-space missions: communication delays of up to **20 minutes** between astronauts and Mission Control. During this delay, immediate medical guidance from Earth is not always available.
AstroPulse analyzes onboard health indicators across multiple body systems—including cardiovascular health, bone health, muscle condition, radiation exposure, immune response, sleep, mental wellness, and blood clot risk—to provide real-time risk assessments and precautionary guidance. Rather than replacing doctors or Mission Control, the system helps astronauts take safe initial actions while awaiting expert instructions from Earth.
The platform also features interactive dashboards, health trend visualization, anatomy diagrams, and educational references inspired by NASA's Human Research Program. By supporting greater onboard awareness and autonomous decision-making, AstroPulse demonstrates how intelligent software can improve astronaut safety and mission resilience during future long-duration space exploration.
details:
AstroPulse is an AI-assisted educational astronaut health monitoring and decision-support system designed for long-duration space missions. The project addresses one of the most significant operational challenges in deep-space exploration: communication delays of up to 20 minutes between astronauts and Mission Control. During this delay, astronauts may need to respond to health concerns without immediate medical guidance from Earth.

AstroPulse continuously analyzes multiple health domains, including cardiovascular health, bone health, muscle condition, radiation exposure, immune response, sleep quality, mental wellness, and blood clot (VTE) awareness. Using onboard health data, wearable sensor readings, crew inputs, and trend analysis, the application evaluates potential risks and provides immediate precautionary guidance to help astronauts take safe initial actions until Mission Control or the flight surgeon can respond.

The project was developed using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript as a fully responsive single-page web application. Interactive dashboards, SVG-based anatomical illustrations, health trend graphs, and an intuitive user interface were designed to make complex medical information easier to understand during critical situations. Three.js was also integrated to create an immersive space-themed experience.

AstroPulse was designed using publicly available NASA resources, including the NASA Human Research Program (HRP), NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), and NASA-STD-3001 Spaceflight Human-System Standard. These references were used to understand spaceflight health risks and ensure that the educational content reflects current research without reproducing NASA datasets.

The application also considers how health information could realistically be obtained during a mission. Cardiovascular data can originate from wearable biomedical sensors or smart monitoring garments, radiation exposure from personal dosimeters, sleep and mental wellness from wearable devices and crew self-assessments, muscle health from exercise performance data, immune health from laboratory biomarkers, and bone health through portable ultrasound-based assessments combined with trend analysis, since direct bone mineral density scans are not currently performed during spaceflight.

The creativity of AstroPulse lies in combining multiple astronaut health systems into a single onboard decision-support platform while focusing on communication-delay autonomy. Rather than replacing medical professionals, the system provides timely precautionary recommendations that can help astronauts remain informed and prepared during periods when immediate assistance from Earth is unavailable.

By improving onboard awareness, supporting autonomous decision-making, and promoting astronaut safety during communication delays, AstroPulse demonstrates how intelligent software can contribute to the future of long-duration human space exploration.
